[Textbook misprint: the working above has been corrected. The book applies its Eq. (15.23), \(Q = [m_X - m_Y - m_e]c^2\), to ATOMIC masses and prints \(0.002502 \times 931.5 = 2.3306\) MeV. For a beta PLUS decay written with atomic masses two electron masses must be subtracted, not one, because the parent atom carries one more electron than the daughter and a positron is created as well. The book's value is therefore too large by exactly one electron rest energy, \(0.00055 \times 931.5 = 0.512\) MeV. The correct maximum kinetic energy is 1.818 MeV, which agrees with the accepted \(Q(\beta^{+})\) of 1.820 MeV for \(^{22}\text{Na}\).]

The decay can be written as

\(^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \rightarrow {}^{22}_{10}\text{Ne} + e^{+} +\) neutrino

The masses given are ATOMIC masses, so the electrons must be counted. The sodium atom carries 11 electrons and the neon atom only 10, and a positron is created as well, so two electron masses have to be subtracted:

\(Q = \left[m_{Na} - m_{Ne} - 2m_e\right]c^2\)

\(= [21.994437 - 21.991385 - 2 \times 0.00055]c^2\)

\(= [0.003052 - 0.0011]c^2\)

\(= 0.001952 \times 931.5\ \text{MeV} = 1.818\ \text{MeV}\)

The same figure follows from NUCLEAR masses: \(M(\text{Na}) = 21.994437 - 11m_e = 21.988387\) u and \(M(\text{Ne}) = 21.991385 - 10m_e = 21.985885\) u, giving \(Q = [21.988387 - 21.985885 - 0.00055] \times 931.5 = 1.818\ \text{MeV}\).

This is the maximum energy that the beta particle \((e^{+})\) can have, the neutrino having zero energy in that case.

[Textbook misprint: the arithmetic above has been corrected. From the book's own printed inputs, \(236.04557 - 136.91787 - 96.91827 - 2 \times 1.00865 = 0.19213\) u, but the book prints \(0.19011\) u and hence \(177.0875\) MeV. The subtraction is simply wrong: 0.19011 u would require \(m_n = 1.00966\) u, a value the book states nowhere (it uses 1.00865 u in this very example, 1.00866 u in the Exercises data and 1.008665 u in Section 15.7.1). The correct energy released is 178.97 MeV.]

Energy released is given by

\(Q = [m_U - m_I - m_Y - 2m_n]c^2\)

\(= [236.04557 - 136.91787 - 96.91827 - 2 \times 1.00865]c^2\)

Taking the subtractions in turn,

\(236.04557 - 136.91787 = 99.12770\)

\(99.12770 - 96.91827 = 2.20943\)

\(2 \times 1.00865 = 2.01730\)

\(2.20943 - 2.01730 = 0.19213\)

\(\therefore Q = 0.19213 \times 931.5\ \text{MeV} = 178.97\ \text{MeV}\)

(The electrons balance on the two sides, \(92 = 53 + 39\), so the atomic masses may be used directly.)
